learningObjective: Design a shape-coverage matrix for testing a GPU kernel so that the test suite covers boundary shapes, tile-boundary shapes, and typical production shapes.

canonicalClaims.claim: A shape-coverage matrix should include empty shapes, singletons, tile-boundary sizes (tile, tile+1, tile-1), a few large production sizes, and a random-shape fuzz set to catch masked-load boundary bugs and rare corner cases.
conditions: The kernel has a compile-time tile size or fixed vector width.
The kernel uses masked loads/stores at partial tiles.
nonImplications: Does not imply exhaustive testing of every shape.
Does not imply fuzz shapes replace named boundary shapes.

misconceptions.claim: Power-of-two shapes are sufficient for coverage.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Boundary bugs live at non-power-of-two sizes and near tile boundaries.
Empty and singleton shapes catch degenerate-case bugs.

misconceptions.claim: Only current production shapes need testing.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Overfits tests to today's workload; future shape changes will silently break.

misconceptions.claim: Fuzz-only shape coverage replaces named boundary shapes.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Fuzz is probabilistic; named boundaries provide guaranteed coverage of known edge cases.
